question: Does providing native method documentation lead to a concrete source-checkable constraint in proposals for existing candidate pairs?
selection: case_id ascending; exclude ut-tests paths, path.rs, getattr/inode_init and unlink/rmdir methods; require at least one nonempty native method document; select first two cases without reusing any source path from previously selected cases
source_family_caveat: Distinct source files are not certified semantic independence; both cases remain exposed development data
contexts: Exact two archived function snippets plus path and source line metadata; reject snippets containing comments or doc attributes instead of inventing a stripping frontend. Full files reserved for post-output evidence binding, not agents.
agent_policy: Four fresh non-forked agent contexts, same inherited parent model, no tools requested/allowed in task instructions, no old labels/ranks/results, one response per context, at most 900 Chinese characters excluding code identifiers
isolation_limit: Instruction-level no-tools constraint, not OS sandbox isolation; exact inference token budget, seed and model revision are not controlled. Do not describe this as equal-compute causal evaluation.
outputs: shared mechanism proposal or reasoned abstention
measurement: Retain four raw outputs; manually bind concrete claims to fixed full source after outputs. Separate code-visible constraints, documentation-only declarations, source-supported additions, unsupported inferences and unknowns. No accuracy denominator or weighted quality score.
stop: Four responses and evidence binding, including zero-increment or no-proposal outcomes; no prompt tuning, replacement cases, or new verifier development.
limits: not behavior equivalence or adoption benefit
native-doc effect is not completed-contract-doc effect
